author: ohtadmin
title: Architect outlines 7 changes for Getty
text:
A slightly reorganized Fort Getty could free about 4 acres of currently utilized land to open space, according to landscape architect Arek Galle.
A recap of the schematic plan was presented Tuesday to the ad hoc committee charged with exploring ways to improve the 41-acre park.
Galle, a senior associate with BETA group, has been working with the committee since August.
“We’ve talked a lot about underutilized land, reclaiming land and sort of re-evaluating land use,” Galle said.
Seven key actions were presented to achieve Galle’s proposal, which includes “generally retaining the current park programming” while formalizing a “vision and approach” to the park.
The actions include positioning all tent camping to the lot near the gatehouse; eliminating the fragmentation of RV sites; expanding the perimeter of open space at the water’s edge; reclaiming underutilized land; improving walkability and connectivity; organizing vehicular circulation and parking; and realigning the roads.
“Let’s develop a concept of a loop road that sort of defines where the RVs will be and sort of opens the door for the public to use the perimeter freely,” Galle said.
These actions would allow about an acre of upper tent camping to become open space. Reducing the RV park from 75 sites to 62 would help free about another 2 acres in that area.
By reclaiming Battery Tousard, moreover, a fourth acre of park space could be achieved.
“Among the most striking findings of the committee’s work was the opportunity presented by the area above Battery Tousard, at the center of the park,” the committee says in its drafted report. “Currently overgrown and inaccessible to most visitors, the summit offers panoramic views of Narragansett Bay, Dutch Island and the surrounding landscape. Opening and making this area accessible would deliver an immediate, meaningful improvement to the park experience.”
The trailer park currently covers about 4.1 acres with each site averaging about 2,435 square feet. One of Galle’s proposals, which includes unified 36-by-60-foot sites, would consolidate all campers within the loop road, reducing the campground’s footprint by about 21,780 square feet.
Galle’s plan would create larger, more contiguous greenspace while developing looping, interconnected walking paths between attractions. He also wants to restore habitat, manage invasive species, plant shade trees and shrubs, and create view corridors.
summary: A slightly reorganized Fort Getty could free about 4 acres of currently utilized land to open space, according to landscape architect Arek Galle. A recap of the schematic plan was presented Tuesday to the ad hoc committee charged with exploring ways to improve the 41-acre park. The actions include positioning all tent camping to the lot near the gatehouse; eliminating the fragmentation of RV sites; expanding the perimeter of open space at the water’s edge; reclaiming underutilized land; improving walkability and connectivity; organizing vehicular circulation and parking; and realigning the roads.
